concept.name: Delivery versus payment
concept.definition: A securities settlement mechanism that links the transfer of securities to the transfer of funds so that delivery occurs if and only if payment occurs, eliminating principal risk — the risk of delivering securities without receiving the money, or vice versa.
concept.intuition: The shares and the cash swap hands atomically: neither side can end up having given away its asset without receiving the other side of the deal.
concept.mechanics: The settlement system conditions the final transfer of securities on the final transfer of funds within the same process (e.g., DTC book-entry delivery against a simultaneous settlement debit/credit); models range from gross-gross (DvP model 1) to net-net (DvP model 3) in BIS terminology.
concept.failure_modes: DvP removes principal risk but not liquidity or replacement-cost risk: a counterparty can still fail to deliver, forcing a buy-in, and gridlock can arise when participants wait for incoming securities to fund outgoing deliveries.
concept.misconceptions: DvP does not guarantee the trade happens — it guarantees that if one leg settles, the other does too; a failed trade under DvP simply does not settle either leg.
concept.example: When an investor's share purchase settles T+1 at DTC, the seller's account is credited cash and debited shares in the same settlement pass, so the seller never parts with the stock unpaid.

citations.source: BIS CPMI, Glossary of payments and market infrastructure terminology
